recall_prompt: Say how you would find the mean deviation about the mean for six numbers — what you find first and what you average at the end.
insider_note: n = 6 counts the repeated 10 twice and divides both steps; the answer 16/6 = 2.666… is written 2.67, the two-decimal form this chapter uses.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Mean
steps.margin_note: First mark. Six values, sum 42, mean 7. Write n = 6 — it is the divisor in both steps.

recall.must_convey: That the mean of the six values is 42/6 = 7.
accept: add the six numbers to get forty two and divide by six, the mean is seven
x bar is forty two by six equals seven
the mean of the data is seven
aaru numbers add cheste forty two, six tho divide cheste mean seven
sum forty two, n six, mean seven

steps.why: Mean deviation is measured from the mean, so the mean has to exist first. The signed deviations from the mean add to zero, which is why the next step drops the signs.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 5 because 10 appears twice — n counts every value, so n = 6.

steps.label: Mean deviation
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the six absolute deviations, add them (16), divide by n = 6. 16/6 = 2.666…, written 2.67.

recall.must_convey: That the absolute deviations from 7 are 4, 1, 3, 3, 2, 3, their sum 16 divided by 6 gives 2.67.
accept: take each number minus seven without sign, four one three three two three, add to sixteen, divide by six, two point six seven
the absolute deviations add to sixteen and sixteen by six is two point six seven
mean deviation is sigma mod x i minus x bar by n equals sixteen by six equals two point six seven
seven nunchi deviations mod teesukoni add cheste sixteen, six tho divide cheste two point six seven
the answer is two point six seven

steps.why: Mean deviation is the average distance from the mean. The absolute value is what stops the distances cancelling — without it the total is 0 for every data set.
common_mistakes: Dividing 16 by 5 or by 7 instead of by n = 6.
